page: Amazon Web Services m5a.2xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.5 GHz, it provides 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation stands at 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Storage is omitted locally, requiring network-attached storage for non-volatile data persistence. Baseline network throughput is configured at 2 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates moderate performance typical for its processor generation. PassMark tests yielded average results for overall CPU score (6871.6), memory score (1926.66), and encryption throughput (6484.1). However, raw single-core and multi-core processing speeds in stress-ng and Geekbench fell into lower tiers, with a single-core Geekbench score of 729. Memory bandwidth reaches 27.54 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, while Redis SET operations achieved 4.98 million operations per second. For lightweight LLM tasks using a 135M parameter model, text generation reached 85.6 tokens per second, dropping to 5.02 tokens per second on a 7B model.

The hardware profile offers a cost-effective alternative to higher-frequency general-purpose instances, delivering predictable resource density with 32 GB of RAM on an 8 vCPU dedicated allocation. Tradeoffs include lower single-threaded compute speeds and the absence of local NVMe storage or advanced AVX-512 instruction set extensions. This instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads such as web servers, microservices, small-scale caching layers, and background processing tasks that benefit from dedicated vCPUs and balanced memory without requiring intensive vector computations.
description: Amazon Web Services m5a.2xlarge is a general-purpose cloud server powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.5 GHz under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 4 physical cores supplying 8 dedicated vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading, alongside 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio. The instance lacks local ephemeral storage and relies on external storage options, while offering a baseline network speed of 2 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks reveal average results for PassMark CPU and memory scores alongside encryption performance, though single-core compute and uncached memory bandwidth fall in lower benchmark percentiles. The hardware offers predictable resource density for cost-sensitive environments. Lacking AVX-512 support, the m5a.2xlarge serves general-purpose application tiers, moderate web serving, Redis caching, microservice hosting, and lightweight software compilation tasks requiring predictable dedicated core allocations.
